39949166.patient_population: adolescents undergoing hand-wrist radiography for bone age assessment (public RSNA dataset and an in-house dataset)
39949166.model_description: Given a hand-wrist radiograph, a U-Net first automatically localizes the regions of interest used in the Tanner-Whitehouse method, then an InceptionResNetV2 network extracts features from both the regions of interest and the whole image to estimate bone age, combining the region-based (TW3) and whole-image (Greulich-Pyle) approaches. 39949166.headline_result: Localization precision of 99.1% on the public RSNA dataset; mean absolute error 0.38 years (males) and 0.45 years (females) on RSNA, and 0.41 years (males) and 0.44 years (females) on the in-house dataset.

40987805.model_family: deep learning bone age model (Deeplasia) with sex-specific linear recalibration
40987805.patient_population: Georgian children undergoing hand radiography for bone age assessment (retrospective cohort of 381 pediatric hand radiographs)
40987805.model_description: The model takes a hand radiograph and outputs an estimated bone age. The existing open-source deep learning tool Deeplasia was recalibrated with a sex-specific linear correction fit on 121 Georgian children's hand radiographs, rated by seven local pediatric radiologists and endocrinologists, to produce Deeplasia-GE, then tested on a held-out set of 260 images.
40987805.dataset_size: 381 pediatric hand radiographs (121 used for calibration, 260 held out for testing)
40987805.headline_result: Calibration reduced mean absolute difference from 6.57 to 5.69 months on the held-out test set (n=260); Deeplasia-GE had smaller error than any of the individual human raters.

41258793.clinical_problem: normative pediatric kidney size (length and volume) reference values
41258793.patient_population: children from birth to 18 years undergoing renal ultrasound at a tertiary children's hospital, 2012-2022
41258793.model_description: An NLP model extracted kidney length and volume measurements from the text of 24,664 pediatric ultrasound reports (18,769 children, birth to 18 years). These extracted measurements were combined with anthropometric data and modeled with age-adjusted quantile regression to generate new normative percentiles for kidney length and volume by age and body surface area, using the lambda-mu-sigma (LMS) method.
41258793.headline_result: Kidney growth was most pronounced in the first year of life (length +1.8 cm, volume +16.9 cm3); body surface area was a better predictor of kidney volume than age (R1=0.57 vs 0.48, P<.001); standard errors were 10%-30% lower than prior normative values.

41321009.model_description: Three commercial AI products (YIZHUN-TW3, LIANYING-TW3, AIBAA-TW3) each take a hand-wrist radiograph and output a bone age using the Tanner-Whitehouse 3 (TW3) method. Their readings were compared against a manual TW3 reading and a reference standard across age groups 3-17 years using linear regression and Bland-Altman analysis.
41321009.release_evidence: named vendor products (YIZHUN-TW3, LIANYING-TW3, AIBAA-TW3) compared as commercial bone age assessment software
41321009.dataset_size: children aged 3-17 years (case count not stated)
41321009.headline_result: YIZHUN-TW3 and LIANYING-TW3 showed R2=0.9861 versus the reference standard; AIBAA-TW3 R2=0.9591; manual-TW3 R2=0.9732; AIBAA-TW3 underestimated bone age with a mean difference of -0.69 years.
